LESSON: IMITATIVE SPEAKING: PRONUNCIATION

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.8: Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 6 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How can we take care of our immediate environment? 2. Why do we use imitative speaking to learn languages?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. team up to describe weather conditions using appropriate pronunciation and intonation,

2. listen keenly to a presentation on weather conditions,

3. work with peers to answer questions based on the presentation,

4. play a language game involving describing weather patterns using non-verbal cues and have peers guess the weather condition implied. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. team up to describe weather conditions using appropriate pronunciation and intonation,
2. listen keenly to a presentation on weather conditions,
3. work with peers to answer questions based on the presentation,
4. play a language game involving describing weather patterns using non-verbal cues and have peers guess the weather condition implied. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner contributes to group decision making when describing

weather conditions using appropriate pronunciation and intonation

• Critical thinking and problem solving: This is promoted as the learner analyses concepts by logical reasoning when

answering questions based on the presentation.

using non-verbal cues and has peers guess the weather condition implied.

Link to Other Learning Areas:
